cards.q: What is a Bloom filter?
cards.a: A space-efficient probabilistic data structure used to test whether an element is a member of a set.

cards.q: What are the two possible answers returned by a Bloom filter query?
cards.a: "Possibly in set" or "definitely not in set".

cards.q: Which Bloom filter variant addresses the inability to remove elements?
What is an empty Bloom filter?
cards.a: A bit array of m bits, all set to 0.

cards.q: What do the k hash functions of a Bloom filter do?
cards.a: Map set elements to one of the m possible array positions.

cards.q: What happens to the probability of false positives as more items are added to a Bloom filter?
In Bloom's hyphenation example, why do the remaining 10% of words matter?
cards.a: They require expensive disk accesses to retrieve specific hyphenation patterns.

cards.q: For optimality, which two properties should a Bloom filter's hash functions have?
cards.a: They should be uniformly distributed and independent.

cards.q: What does the choice of k in a Bloom filter depend on?
cards.a: The desired false error rate ε; k is typically a small constant.

cards.q: What is m, the Bloom filter's bit-array size, proportional to?
cards.a: k and the number of elements to be added.

cards.q: How is an element added to a Bloom filter?
cards.a: Feed it to each of the k hash functions to get k array positions, then set the bits at all these positions to 1.

cards.q: When testing an element in a Bloom filter, what does a 0 at any of the k positions prove?
cards.a: That the element is definitely not in the set.

A Bloom filter hash area of what relative size still eliminates 87% of disk accesses?
cards.a: Only 18% of the size needed by an ideal error-free hash.

cards.q: How many bits per element are required for a 1% false positive probability in a Bloom filter?
cards.a: Fewer than 10 bits per element, independent of the size or number of elements in the set.

cards.q: Are false negatives possible in a Bloom filter?
cards.a: No — false positive matches are possible, but false negatives are not.

cards.q: Can elements be removed from a standard Bloom filter?
cards.a: No; elements can be added to the set but not removed.
